# fortiappseccloud_waf_template_waiting_room

Configures waiting room for one FortiAppSec Cloud WAF template using the static template endpoint `/waf/template/{template_id}/waiting_room`. This resource owns the template's module settings. To make an application inherit them, configure the matching app module resource with `template = true` and omit its `configs` block.

Declare only one `fortiappseccloud_waf_template_waiting_room` resource for a WAF template.

## Example Usage

```hcl
resource "fortiappseccloud_waf_template_waiting_room" "example" {
  template_id = fortiappseccloud_waf_template.example.template_id

  configs {
    status                    = true
    path                      = "/.*"
    enable_total_active_users = true
    total_active_users        = 1000
    enable_new_users_per_min  = false
    new_users_per_min         = 60
    session_duration          = 5
    custom_wt_page            = "Predefined"

    bypass_rules {
      item {
        rule_type  = "source-ip"
        rule_value = "192.0.2.10"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

- `template_id` (Required, Forces replacement) — WAF template ID.
- `configs` (Required) — Typed waiting room configuration. Its attributes and ownership-wrapper blocks are identical to `fortiappseccloud_waf_waiting_room` when that app resource uses `template = false`.

## Import

Import using the template ID:

```shell
terraform import fortiappseccloud_waf_template_waiting_room.example TEMPLATE_ID
```

The first read after import hydrates all supported ownership wrappers.

## Destroy Behavior
Destroy performs a fresh GET, preserves the complete response, sets `template=false` and `configs.status=false`, sends the complete PUT, and verifies the normalized GET response before Terraform removes the resource from state.
